children: Sovereign PPG, the region’s leading business formation and corporate services provider, has secured a licence to operate within the Qatar Financial Centre (QFC), expanding its ability to support regulated, specialist and cross-border business activity in the gas-rich country.

The new licence builds on Sovereign PPG’s established presence in both the Qatar Free Zones (QFZ) and Qatar’s mainland commercial regime, giving the company access to a distinct segment of Qatar’s financial and corporate ecosystem.

Through its dedicated QFC entity, Sovereign PPG offers clients a flexible corporate platform for establishing regional headquarters and service-based entities, as well as structuring cross-border activities.

The QFC provides 100% foreign ownership, streamlined compliance and access to Qatar’s expanding network of double tax treaties. Its internationally aligned legal and regulatory framework also strengthens Sovereign PPG’s ability to support cross-border mandates efficiently, said the statement.

The expansion enables Sovereign PPG to support a broader range of sophisticated corporate and regulated mandates, including financial institutions, investment and advisory businesses, special purpose vehicles (SPVs) and multinational businesses establishing regional operations.

This complements its existing Qatar capabilities, allowing Sovereign PPG to support clients with different regulatory, governance and operational requirements through the most appropriate jurisdiction.

The new QFC capability also strengthens Sovereign PPG’s ability to support multi-jurisdictional strategies across the Gulf. Companies establishing regional headquarters, governance structures and other specialist functions in Qatar can use the QFC as part of a wider regional structure while building commercial relationships in other GCC markets. Sovereign PPG supports these clients with QFC-based corporate governance, compliance and corporate secretarial services, alongside wider HR and operational support where appropriate.

On the new licence, Managing Director Neil Wilson said: "The QFC licence gives us a robust, internationally-aligned framework to support cross-border advisory, consulting and corporate services efficiently."

"Our existing presence in QFZ and the mainland gives us a strong operational base in Qatar, while the QFC opens access to a different segment of the market and enables us to support more complex and specialised mandates. It strengthens our ability to support clients establishing a regulatory base in Qatar and expanding across the Gulf," he added.

Operating across both the Ministry of Commerce & Industry (MOCI) regime and the QFC gives Sovereign PPG the flexibility to meet different client needs. Clients can establish on-the-ground operations through Qatar’s domestic commercial regime or use a QFC platform for international transactions, regulated activities and eligible advisory mandates, with Sovereign PPG supporting them from setup through ongoing compliance.

Sovereign PPG’s expansion in Qatar comes as the country targets US$100 billion in foreign direct investment by 2030 and continues to strengthen its international investment appeal. Qatar’s Third National Development Strategy (NDS3) reinforces this direction, with a focus on competitive economic clusters, a stronger business environment, innovation and foreign investment.

The QFC’s internationally aligned framework and business environment provide an additional platform for international clients seeking to establish or grow their operations in Qatar and across the Gulf. Key benefits include a flat 10% corporate tax rate on locally sourced profits and 100% repatriation of profits, dividends, interest, royalties and management fees.

Sovereign PPG brings deep experience across multiple GCC jurisdictions, including Dubai International Financial Centre (DIFC), Abu Dhabi Global Market (ADGM) and mainland structures. This regional perspective enables the company to guide clients through the legal, regulatory and operational complexities of establishing and scaling across the Gulf.

“For international clients looking to establish a presence in the Gulf, the QFC offers a familiar and flexible legal environment,” Wilson noted. “We help navigate the setup process end-to-end, ensuring their structure is compliant, tax-efficient and scalable,” he added.
